claim: Angelopoulos & Bates' tutorial restates Tibshirani et al.'s weighted-conformal-under-covariate-shift result as their Theorem 3 and explicitly labels it a restricted case that requires the covariate shift (density ratio) to be known, not merely estimated.
stance_target: treating the weighted-exchangeability/covariate-shift conformal guarantee as unconditionally valid regardless of whether the density ratio is known or estimated
scope_conditions: split and full conformal prediction under covariate shift
quoted_support: This algorithm addresses a somewhat restricted case—that of a known covariate shift—but is nonetheless quite practical.

claim: The tutorial generalizes to distribution drift and states that weighted conformal procedures always satisfy marginal coverage as an upper bound property, but are only EXACT (i.e., achieve the nominal 1-alpha coverage tightly) when the magnitude of the distribution shift is known.
stance_target: a claim that estimating the weights still yields the exact same marginal-validity guarantee as using true weights
scope_conditions: weighted conformal prediction under general distribution shift/drift
quoted_support: The following theory provides some justification for such weighted conformal procedures; in particular, they always satisfy marginal coverage, and are exact when the magnitude of the distribution shift is known.
